distinguishing_features: Applies gas-phase chemical-potential control to a turbine TBC/bond-coat oxidation problem rather than to reactor-wall deposition/fouling.
Injects a volatile halogenated oxidizing precursor into dilution/secondary air to locally raise oxidizing potential at the coated surface.
Targets rapid in-situ formation of a dense alpha-Al2O3 scale before transient CTE shear exceeds interfacial strength.
Uses dilution-air telemetry-derived dosing and an oxide-thickness threshold rather than Mg-feed/temperature-setpoint retuning.
parsed.objective_technical_problem: How to reduce early-life TBC spallation caused by delayed or defective protective alumina formation and CTE mismatch in turbine blades without redesigning the bond-coat alloy.
parsed.viable_reason: The additive is injected into dilution air that cannot reliably contact the buried bond coat, CF4/fluorinated species are not benign oxidizers and would likely corrode or contaminate the TBC system, and the asserted 10^4 increase in kp producing dense alpha-Al2O3 is unsupported.
parsed.non_obvious_reason: Prior art 1 only teaches lowering wall reactant chemical potential by Mg feed and temperature changes to suppress deposition, not injecting halogenated oxidizers to accelerate protective alumina formation on a TBC bond coat.
